<h1 id="lob-qr-codes">QR Codes</h1>


Lob QR codes allow you to generate a QR code that is unique to each mailpiece, thereby allowing each and every customers to receive a personalized link. See the Create endpoint for <a href="#tag/Letters/operation/letter_create">Letters</a>, <a href="#tag/Postcards/operation/postcard_create">Postcards</a> or <a href="#tag/Self-Mailers/operation/self_mailer_create">Self Mailers</a> to learn how to embed a QR code into your mail piece.

Webhooks can be used to integrate Lob QR code scans into your omni channel marketing strategy. See the <a href="#tag/Webhooks">Webhooks</a> section of our documentation to learn how to enable the `letter.viewed`, `postcard.viewed` and `self_mailer.viewed` event notifications for your mail pieces.

Furthermore, our QR code Analytics endpoint can be used to track the impact and engagement rate of your mail sends. Lob can tell you exactly which recipients opened your mailpiece. Our Analytics endpoint allows you to see exactly which recipient scanned a mailpiece, when they scanned it, and more!

<div class="back-to-top" ><a href="#" onclick="toTopLink()">back to top</a></div>


## List

<a id="opIdqr_codes_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/qr_code_analytics \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /qr_code_analytics`

Returns a list of your QR codes. The QR codes are returned sorted by scan date, with the most recently scanned QR codes appearing first.

<h3 id="list-10-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|How many results to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|An integer that designates the offset at which to begin returning results. Defaults to 0.|
|include|query|[string]|false|Request that the response include the total count by specifying `include=["total_count"]`.<br>|
|date_created|query|[date_filter](#schemadate_filter)|false|Filter by date created. Accepted formats are ISO-8601 date or datetime, e.g. `{ "gt": "2012-01-01", "lt": "2012-01-31T12:34:56Z" }` where `gt` is >, `lt` is <, `gte` is ≥, and `lte` is ≤.|
|scanned|query|boolean|false|Filter list of responses to only include QR codes with at least one scan event.|
|resource_ids|query|array|false|Filter by the resource ID.|

<h3 id="list-10-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a list of QR Codes and their analytics.|None|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="lob-resource-proofs">Resource Proofs</h1>

The resource proofs endpoint allows you to create a final rendering of any template. This is best practice to ensure that you are visually validating your creative before any mail pieces use the template. The API provides endpoints for creating, updating, and retrieving template proofs.
<div class="back-to-top" ><a href="#" onclick="toTopLink()">back to top</a></div>

<h1 id="lob-reverse-geocode-lookups">Reverse Geocode Lookups</h1>

Find a list of zip codes associated with a valid US location via latitude and longitude. <br> <div class="back-to-top" ><a href="#" onclick="toTopLink()">back to top</a></div>


## Reverse Geocode Lookup

<a id="opIdreverse_geocode_lookup"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/us_reverse_geocode_lookups \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "latitude": 37.7749,
    "longitude": 122.4194
  }'
```

`POST /us_reverse_geocode_lookups`

Reverse geocode a valid US location with a live API key.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "latitude": 37.7749,
  "longitude": 122.4194
}
```

<h3 id="reverse-geocode-lookup-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|size|query|integer|false|Determines the number of locations returned. Possible values are between 1 and 50 and any number higher will be rounded down to 50. Default size is a list of 5 reverse geocoded locations.|
|body|body|[location](#schemalocation)|true|none|
|» latitude|body|number(float) \| null|true|A positive or negative decimal indicating the geographic latitude of the address, specifying the north-to-south position of a location. This should be input with `longitude` to pinpoint locations on a map.<br>|
|» longitude|body|number(float) \| null|true|A positive or negative decimal indicating the geographic longitude of the address, specifying the north-to-south position of a location. This should be input with `latitude` to pinpoint locations on a map.<br>|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "us_reverse_geocode_8a013f3e",
  "addresses": [
    {
      "components": {
        "zip_code": "94107",
        "zip_code_plus_4": "1702"
      },
      "location_analysis": {
        "latitude": 37.78271,
        "longitude": -122.416202,
        "distance": 1.32
      }
    },
    {
      "components": {
        "zip_code": "94107",
        "zip_code_plus_4": "1702"
      },
      "location_analysis": {
        "latitude": 37.782917,
        "longitude": -122.416131,
        "distance": 1.33
      }
    }
  ]
}
```

> default Response

```json

  "error": {
    "code": "invalid",
    "message": "latitude is required",
    "status_code": 422
  }
}
```

<h3 id="reverse-geocode-lookup-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|

|200|OK|Returns a zip lookup object if a valid zip was provided.|[reverse_geocode](#schemareverse_geocode)|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

|Status|Header|Type|Format|Description|

|200|ratelimit-remaining|integer||The number of requests remaining in the current window.|

<h1 id="lob-self-mailers">Self Mailers</h1>

The self mailer endpoint allows you to easily print and mail self mailers. The API provides endpoints
for creating self mailers, retrieving individual self mailers, canceling self mailers, and retrieving a list of self mailers.
<div class="back-to-top" ><a href="#" onclick="toTopLink()">back to top</a></div>


## Retrieve

<a id="opIdself_mailer_retrieve"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/self_mailers/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /self_mailers/{sfm_id}`

Retrieves the details of an existing self_mailer. You need only supply the unique self_mailer identifier that was returned upon self_mailer creation.

<h3 id="retrieve-14-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sfm_id|path|[sfm_id](#schemasfm_id)|true|id of the self_mailer|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "not_found",
    "message": "to address not found",
    "status_code": 404
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-14-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a self_mailer object|None|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Delete

<a id="opIdself_mailer_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/self_mailers/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /self_mailers/{sfm_id}`

Completely removes a self mailer from production. This can only be done if the self mailer's `send_date` has not yet passed. If the self mailer is successfully canceled, you will not be charged for it. This feature is exclusive to certain customers. Upgrade to the appropriate <a href="https://dashboard.lob.com/#/settings/editions" target="_blank">Print & Mail Edition</a> to gain access.

<h3 id="delete-5-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|sfm_id|path|[sfm_id](#schemasfm_id)|true|id of the self_mailer|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "sfm_123456789",
  "deleted": true
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "not_found",
    "message": "to address not found",
    "status_code": 404
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-5-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Deleted|[self_mailer_deletion](#schemaself_mailer_deletion)|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## List

<a id="opIdself_mailers_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/self_mailers \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /self_mailers`

Returns a list of your self_mailers. The self_mailers are returned sorted by creation date, with the most recently created self_mailers appearing first.

<h3 id="list-11-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|How many results to return.|
|before/after|query|object|false|`before` and `after` are both optional but only one of them can be in the query at a time.<br>|
|include|query|[string]|false|Request that the response include the total count by specifying `include=["total_count"]`.<br>|
|date_created|query|[date_filter](#schemadate_filter)|false|Filter by date created. Accepted formats are ISO-8601 date or datetime, e.g. `{ "gt": "2012-01-01", "lt": "2012-01-31T12:34:56Z" }` where `gt` is >, `lt` is <, `gte` is ≥, and `lte` is ≤.|
|metadata|query|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|Filter by metadata key-value pair`.|
|size|query|[[self_mailer_size](#schemaself_mailer_size)]|false|The self mailer sizes to be returned.|
|scheduled|query|boolean|false|* `true` - only return orders (past or future) where `send_date` is<br>greater than `date_created`<br>* `false` - only return orders where `send_date` is equal to `date_created`<br>|
|send_date|query|[send_date](#schemasend_date)|false|Filter by ISO-8601 date or datetime, e.g. `{ "gt": "2012-01-01", "lt": "2012-01-31T12:34:56Z" }` where `gt` is >, `lt` is <, `gte` is ≥, and `lte` is ≤.<br>|
|mail_type|query|[mail_type](#schemamail_type)|false|A string designating the mail postage type: * `usps_first_class` - (default) * `usps_standard` - a <a href="https://lob.com/pricing/print-mail#compare" target="_blank">cheaper option</a> which is less predictable and takes longer to deliver. `usps_standard` cannot be used with `4x6` postcards or for any postcards sent outside of the United States.<br>|
|sort_by|query|object|false|Sorts items by ascending or descending dates. Use either `date_created` or `send_date`, not both.<br>|
|campaign_id|query|[campaign_id](#schemacampaign_id)|false|Filters resources created by the provided campaign id, prefixed with `cmp_`. In the case of snap packs, booklets, and letters with size `us_legal`, however, the campaign id is prefixed with `camp_` instead of `cmp_`.|
|status|query|[status](#schemastatus)|false|A string describing the render status:<br>* `processed` - the rendering process is currently underway.<br>* `rendered` - the rendering process has completed successfully.<br>* `failed` - the rendering process has failed.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|size|6x18_bifold|
|size|11x9_bifold|
|size|12x9_bifold|
|size|17.75x9_trifold|
|mail_type|usps_first_class|
|mail_type|usps_standard|
|status|processed|
|status|rendered|
|status|failed|

<h3 id="list-11-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A dictionary with a data property that contains an array of up to `limit` self_mailers. Each entry in the array is a separate self_mailer. The previous and next page of self_mailers can be retrieved by calling the endpoint contained in the `previous_url` and `next_url` fields in the API response respectively.<br>If no more self_mailers are available beyond the current set of returned results, the `next_url` field will be empty.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-11-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object|[object](#schemaobject)|false|none|Value is resource type.|
|next_url|string \| null|false|none|Url of next page of items in list.|
|previous_url|string \| null|false|none|Url of previous page of items in list.|
|count|[count](#schemacount)|false|none|number of resources in a set|
|total_count|integer|false|none|Indicates the total number of records. Provided when the request specifies an "include" query parameter|
|data|[[self_mailer](#schemaself_mailer)]|false|none|list of self_mailers|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Create

<a id="opIdself_mailer_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/self_mailers \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Demo Self Mailer job",
    "to": "adr_bae820679f3f536b",
    "from": "adr_210a8d4b0b76d77b",
    "inside": "https://lob.com/selfmailerinside.pdf",
    "outside": "https://lob.com/selfmaileroutside.pdf",
    "size": "12x9_bifold",
    "metadata": {
      "spiffy": "true"
    },
    "mail_type": "usps_standard",
    "merge_variables": {
      "name": "Harry"
    },
    "send_date": "2017-11-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "use_type": "marketing",
    "qr_code": {
      "position": "relative",
      "redirect_url": "https://www.lob.com",
      "width": "2.5",
      "top": "2.5",
      "right": "2.5",
      "pages": "inside,outside"
    },
    "fsc": true,
    "print_speed": "core"
  }'
```

`POST /self_mailers`

Creates a new self_mailer given information

> Body parameter

```json

<h3 id="create-14-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|A string of no longer than 256 characters that uniquely identifies this resource. For more help integrating idempotency keys, refer to our <a href="https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/building-a-mail-strategy/managing-mail-settings#idempotent-requests-12" target="_blank">implementation guide</a>.<br>|
|idempotency_key|query|string|false|A string of no longer than 256 characters that uniquely identifies this resource. For more help integrating idempotency keys, refer to our <a href="https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/building-a-mail-strategy/managing-mail-settings#idempotent-requests-12" target="_blank">implementation guide</a>.<br>|
|body|body|[self_mailer_editable](#schemaself_mailer_editable)|true|none|
|» description|body|[resource_description](#schemaresource_description)|false|An internal description that identifies this resource. Must be no longer than 255 characters.<br>|
|» metadata|body|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|Use metadata to store custom information for tagging and labeling back to your internal systems. Must be an object with up to 20 key-value pairs. Keys must be at most 40 characters and values must be at most 500 characters. Neither can contain the characters `"` and `\`. i.e. '{"customer_id" : "NEWYORK2015"}' Nested objects are not supported.  See [Metadata](#section/Metadata) for more information.|
|» mail_type|body|[mail_type](#schemamail_type)|false|A string designating the mail postage type:<br>* `usps_first_class` - (default)<br>* `usps_standard` - a <a href="https://lob.com/pricing/print-mail#compare" target="_blank">cheaper option</a> which is<br>less predictable and takes longer to deliver. `usps_standard` cannot be used with `4x6`<br>postcards or for any postcards sent outside of the United States.<br>|
|» merge_variables|body|[merge_variables](#schemamerge_variables)|false|You can input a merge variable payload object to your template or QR code redirect URLs to render dynamic content. For example, if you have a template like: `{{variable_name}}`, pass in `{"variable_name": "Harry"}` to render `Harry`. `merge_variables` must be an object. Any type of value is accepted as long as the object is valid JSON; you can use `strings`, `numbers`, `booleans`, `arrays`, `objects`, or `null`. The max length of the object is 25,000 characters. If you call `JSON.stringify` on your object, it can be no longer than 25,000 characters. Your variable names cannot contain any whitespace or any of the following special characters: `!`, `"`, `#`, `%`, `&`, `'`, `(`, `)`, `*`, `+`, `,`, `/`, `;`, `<`, `=`, `>`, `@`, `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, `` ` ``, `{`, `\|`, `}`, `~`. More instructions can be found in <a href="https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/designing-mail-creatives/dynamic-personalization#using-html-and-merge-variables-10" target="_blank">our guide to using html and merge variables</a>. Depending on your <a href="https://dashboard.lob.com/#/settings/account" target="_blank">Merge Variable strictness</a> setting, if you define variables in your HTML but do not pass them here, you will either receive an error or the variable will render as an empty string. These settings only apply on HTML templates and not on QR code redirect URLs.|
|» send_date|body|[send_date](#schemasend_date)|false|A timestamp in ISO 8601 format which specifies a date after the current time and up to 180 days in the future to send the letter off for production. Setting a send date overrides the default [cancellation window](#section/Cancellation-Windows) applied to the mailpiece. Until the `send_date` has passed, the mailpiece can be canceled. If a date in the format `2017-11-01` is passed, it will evaluate to midnight UTC of that date (`2017-11-01T00:00:00.000Z`). If a datetime is passed, that exact time will be used. A `send_date` passed with no time zone will default to UTC, while a `send_date` passed with a time zone will be converted to UTC.|
|» print_speed|body|[print_speed](#schemaprint_speed)|false|A string designating the mail speed type:<br>* `core` - 2 production business days<br>|
|» size|body|[self_mailer_size](#schemaself_mailer_size)|false|Specifies the size of the self mailer. The `17.75x9_trifold` size is in beta. Contact support@lob.com or your account contact to learn more.|
|» to|body|[adr_id](#schemaadr_id) \| [inline_address](#schemainline_address)|true|Must either be an address ID or an inline object with correct address parameters. If an object is used, an address will be created, corrected, and standardized for free whenever possible using our US Address Verification engine (if it is a US address), and returned back with an ID. Depending on your <a href="https://dashboard.lob.com/#/settings/editions" target="_blank">Print & Mail Edition</a>, US addresses may also be run through <a href="#tag/National-Change-of-Address">National Change of Address Linkage(NCOALink)</a>. Non-US addresses will be standardized into uppercase only. If a US address used does not meet your account’s <a href="https://dashboard.lob.com/#/settings/account" target="_blank">US Mail strictness setting</a>, the request will fail. <a href="https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/all-about-addresses" target="_blank">Lob Guide: Verification of Mailing Addresses</a>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[adr_id](#schemaadr_id)|false|Unique identifier prefixed with `adr_`.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[inline_address](#schemainline_address)|false|none|
|» from|body|[adr_id](#schemaadr_id) \| [inline_address_us](#schemainline_address_us)|false|*Required* if `to` address is international. Must either be an address ID or an inline object with correct address parameters. Must either be an address ID or an inline object with correct address parameters. All addresses will be standardized into uppercase without being modified by verification.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[adr_id](#schemaadr_id)|false|Unique identifier prefixed with `adr_`.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[inline_address_us](#schemainline_address_us)|false|none|
|» inside|body|[html_string](#schemahtml_string) \| [tmpl_id](#schematmpl_id) \| [remote_file_url](#schemaremote_file_url) \| [local_file_path](#schemalocal_file_path)|true|The artwork to use as the inside of your self mailer.<br><br>Notes:<br>- HTML merge variables should not include delimiting whitespace.<br>- PDF, PNG, and JPGs must be sized at 6"x18" at 300 DPI, while supplied HTML will be rendered to the specified `size`.<br>- Be sure to leave room for address and postage information by following the templates provided here:<br>  - <a href="https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/public.lob.com/assets/templates/self_mailers/6x18_sfm_bifold_template.pdf" target="_blank">6x18 bifold template</a><br>  - <a href="https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/public.lob.com/assets/templates/self_mailers/12x9_sfm_bifold_template.pdf" target="_blank">12x9 bifold template</a><br>  - <a href="https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/public.lob.com/assets/templates/self_mailers/17_75x9_trifold_sfm_template.pdf" target="_blank">17.75x9 trifold template</a><br><br><br>See [here](#section/HTML-Examples) for HTML examples.<br>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[html_string](#schemahtml_string)|false|An HTML string of under 10,000 characters.|

<h1 id="lob-template-versions">Template Versions</h1>

These API endpoints allow you to create, retrieve, update and delete versions of reusable HTML templates for use with the Print & Mail API.
<div class="back-to-top" ><a href="#" onclick="toTopLink()">back to top</a></div>


## Retrieve

<a id="opIdtemplate_version_retrieve"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/templates/string/versions/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /templates/{tmpl_id}/versions/{vrsn_id}`

Retrieves the template version with the given template and version ids.

<h3 id="retrieve-15-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tmpl_id|path|[tmpl_id](#schematmpl_id)|true|The ID of the template to which the version belongs.|
|vrsn_id|path|[vrsn_id](#schemavrsn_id)|true|id of the template_version|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid",
    "message": "html is required",
    "status_code": 422
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-15-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns the template version with the given template and version ids.|None|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Update

<a id="opIdtemplate_version_update"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/templates/string/versions/string \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Some description"
  }'
```

`POST /templates/{tmpl_id}/versions/{vrsn_id}`

Updates the template version with the given template and version ids.

> Body parameter

{
  "description": "Some description"
}
```

<h3 id="update-7-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|

|vrsn_id|path|[vrsn_id](#schemavrsn_id)|true|id of the template_version|
|body|body|[template_version_updatable](#schematemplate_version_updatable)|true|none|
|» description|body|[resource_description](#schemaresource_description)|false|An internal description that identifies this resource. Must be no longer than 255 characters.<br>|
|» engine|body|[engine](#schemaengine)|false|The engine used to combine HTML template with merge variables.<br>  * `legacy` - Lob's original engine<br>  * `handlebars`<br>|

curl https://api.lob.com/v1/templates/string/versions/string \

  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"

`DELETE /templates/{tmpl_id}/versions/{vrsn_id}`

  "value": {
    "id": "vrsn_123456789",

  }
}
```

    "code": "invalid",
    "message": "html is required",
    "status_code": 422
  }
}

## List

<a id="opIdtemplate_versions_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/templates/string/versions \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /templates/{tmpl_id}/versions`

Returns a list of template versions for the given template ID. The template versions are sorted by creation date, with the most recently created appearing first.


<h3 id="list-12-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tmpl_id|path|[tmpl_id](#schematmpl_id)|true|The ID of the template associated with the retrieved versions|
|limit|query|integer|false|How many results to return.|
|before/after|query|object|false|`before` and `after` are both optional but only one of them can be in the query at a time.<br>|
|include|query|[string]|false|Request that the response include the total count by specifying `include=["total_count"]`.<br>|
|date_created|query|[date_filter](#schemadate_filter)|false|Filter by date created. Accepted formats are ISO-8601 date or datetime, e.g. `{ "gt": "2012-01-01", "lt": "2012-01-31T12:34:56Z" }` where `gt` is >, `lt` is <, `gte` is ≥, and `lte` is ≤.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "data": [
    {
      "id": "vrsn_4d6ff5d868bf630",
      "description": "Second Version",
      "html": "Second HTML for ",
      "date_created": "2017-11-09T05:09:03.665Z",
      "date_modified": "2018-05-22T22:01:10.479Z",
      "object": "version"
    },
    {
      "id": "vrsn_2a17159c1911919",
      "description": "Test Template",
      "html": "HTML for ",
      "date_created": "2017-11-09T05:08:40.004Z",
      "date_modified": "2018-05-22T22:01:11.309Z",
      "object": "version"
    }
  ],
  "object": "list",
  "count": 2
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid",
    "message": "html is required",
    "status_code": 422
  }
}
```

<h3 id="list-12-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A dictionary with a data property that contains an array of up to `limit` template versions. Each entry in the array is a separate template version object. The previous and next page of template versions can be retrieved by calling the endpoint contained in the `previous_url` and `next_url` fields in the API response respectively.<br>If no more template versions are available beyond the current set of returned results, the `next_url` field will be empty.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-12-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object|[object](#schemaobject)|false|none|Value is resource type.|
|next_url|string \| null|false|none|Url of next page of items in list.|
|previous_url|string \| null|false|none|Url of previous page of items in list.|
|count|[count](#schemacount)|false|none|number of resources in a set|
|total_count|integer|false|none|Indicates the total number of records. Provided when the request specifies an "include" query parameter|
|data|[[template_version](#schematemplate_version)]|false|none|list of template versions|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Create

<a id="opIdcreate_template_version"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/templates/string/versions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Some Description",
    "html": "<html>HTML for {{name}}</html>"
  }'
```

`POST /templates/{tmpl_id}/versions`

Creates a new template version attached to the specified template.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Some Description",
  "html": "<html>HTML for {{name}}</html>"
}
```

<h3 id="create-15-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|tmpl_id|path|[tmpl_id](#schematmpl_id)|true|The ID of the template the new version will be attached to|
|body|body|[template_version_writable](#schematemplate_version_writable)|true|none|
|» description|body|[resource_description](#schemaresource_description)|false|An internal description that identifies this resource. Must be no longer than 255 characters.<br>|
|» html|body|[template_html](#schematemplate_html)|true|An HTML string of less than 100,000 characters to be used as the `published_version` of this template. See [here](#section/HTML-Examples) for guidance on designing HTML templates. Please see endpoint specific documentation for any other product-specific HTML details:<br>- [Postcards](#operation/postcard_create) - `front` and `back`<br>- [Self Mailers](#operation/self_mailer_create) - `inside` and `outside`<br>- [Letters](#operation/letter_create) - `file`<br>- [Checks](#operation/check_create) - `check_bottom` and `attachment`<br>- [Cards](#operation/card_create) - `front` and `back`<br><br>If there is a syntax error with your variable names within your HTML, then an error will be thrown, e.g. using a `{{#users}}` opening tag without the corresponding closing tag `{{/users}}`.<br>|
|» engine|body|[engine](#schemaengine)|false|The engine used to combine HTML template with merge variables.<br>  * `legacy` - Lob's original engine<br>  * `handlebars`<br>|
|» required_vars|body|[template_required_vars](#schematemplate_required_vars)|false|An array of required variables to be used in a template. Only available for `handlebars` templates.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» engine|legacy|
|» engine|handlebars|

> Example responses

    "code": "invalid",

  }
}

`GET /templates`

|date_created|query|[date_filter](#schemadate_filter)|false|Filter by date created. Accepted formats are ISO-8601 date or datetime, e.g. `{ "gt": "2012-01-01", "lt": "2012-01-31T12:34:56Z" }` where `gt` is >, `lt` is <, `gte` is ≥, and `lte` is ≤.|

## Create

<a id="opIdcreate_template"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/templates \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "demo",
    "html": "<html>HTML for {{name}}</html>",
    "metadata": {
      "spiffy": "true"
    },
    "engine": "handlebars"
  }'
```

`POST /templates`

Creates a new template for use with the Print & Mail API. In Live mode, you can only have as many non-deleted templates as allotted in your current <a href="https://dashboard.lob.com/#/settings/editions" target="_blank">Print & Mail Edition</a>. If you attempt to create a template past your limit, you will receive a `403` error. There is no limit in Test mode.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "demo",
  "html": "<html>HTML for {{name}}</html>",
  "metadata": {
    "spiffy": "true"
  },
  "engine": "handlebars"
}
```

<h3 id="create-16-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[template_writable](#schematemplate_writable)|true|none|
|» description|body|[resource_description](#schemaresource_description)|false|An internal description that identifies this resource. Must be no longer than 255 characters.<br>|
|» html|body|[template_html](#schematemplate_html)|true|An HTML string of less than 100,000 characters to be used as the `published_version` of this template. See [here](#section/HTML-Examples) for guidance on designing HTML templates. Please see endpoint specific documentation for any other product-specific HTML details:<br>- [Postcards](#operation/postcard_create) - `front` and `back`<br>- [Self Mailers](#operation/self_mailer_create) - `inside` and `outside`<br>- [Letters](#operation/letter_create) - `file`<br>- [Checks](#operation/check_create) - `check_bottom` and `attachment`<br>- [Cards](#operation/card_create) - `front` and `back`<br><br>If there is a syntax error with your variable names within your HTML, then an error will be thrown, e.g. using a `{{#users}}` opening tag without the corresponding closing tag `{{/users}}`.<br>|
|» metadata|body|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|Use metadata to store custom information for tagging and labeling back to your internal systems. Must be an object with up to 20 key-value pairs. Keys must be at most 40 characters and values must be at most 500 characters. Neither can contain the characters `"` and `\`. i.e. '{"customer_id" : "NEWYORK2015"}' Nested objects are not supported.  See [Metadata](#section/Metadata) for more information.|
|» engine|body|[engine](#schemaengine)|false|The engine used to combine HTML template with merge variables.<br>  * `legacy` - Lob's original engine<br>  * `handlebars`<br>|
|» required_vars|body|[template_required_vars](#schematemplate_required_vars)|false|An array of required variables to be used in a template. Only available for `handlebars` templates.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» engine|legacy|
|» engine|handlebars|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid",
    "message": "html is required",
    "status_code": 422
  }
}
```

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a template object|None|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

|200|ratelimit-reset|integer||The time at which the rate limit window resets in  <a href="https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Unix_time" target="_blank">UTC epoch seconds</a><br>|

To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="lob-uploads">Uploads</h1>

The uploads endpoint allows you to upload audience files that are then associated with a given campaign.
At this time, only CSV files are allowed. The API provides endpoints for creating uploads, uploading audience files,
and marking uploaded files as ready for processing. The API also provides endpoints for downloading files that
describe the results, both successful and not, of the processing.

`GET /uploads/{upl_id}/report`

Retrieves the line item data for each row from the csv file associated with the upload id record. NOTE: This endpoint is currently feature flagged. Please reach out to Lob's support team if you  would like access to this API endpoint.

<h3 id="retrieve-line-item-report-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|

|status|query|string|false|The status of line items to filter and retrieve. By default all line items are returned.|
|limit|query|integer|false|How many results to return.|
|offset|query|integer|false|An integer that designates the offset at which to begin returning results. Defaults to 0.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|

|status|Failed|
|status|Processing|

> Example responses

```json
{
  "id": "ex_6a94fe68fd151e0f8",
  "dateCreated": "2021-07-06T22:51:42.838Z",
  "dateModified": "2022-07-06T22:51:42.838Z",
  "deleted": false,
  "s3Url": null,
  "state": "in_progress",
  "type": "failures",
  "uploadId": "upl_71be866e430b11e9"
}
```

> 404 Response

  "error": {
    "code": "not_found",
    "message": "upload not found",
    "status_code": 404
  }
}

|---|---|---|---|

<h3 id="retrieve-line-item-report-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|data|[object]|true|none|none|
|» rowNumber|number|false|none|The row number of the csv file containing this data.|
|» status|string|false|none|The processing status of line item.|
|» errorMessage|string \| null|false|none|The error message detailing the reason why processing the line item failed.|
|» mailpieceId|string \| null|false|none|The mailpiece id created from the line item when it was validated.|
|» originalData|object|false|none|Key-value pairs where each key is the column header and each value is the value of the column for the row.|
|next_url|string \| null|false|none|Url of next page of items in list.|
|prev_url|string \| null|false|none|Url of previous page of items in list.|
|count|[count](#schemacount)|true|none|number of resources in a set|
|total_count|integer|true|none|Indicates the total number of records. Provided when the request specifies an "include" query parameter|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|» status|Validated|
|» status|Failed|
|» status|Processing|

## Retrieve Export

<a id="opIdexport_retrieve"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/uploads/string/exports/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /uploads/{upl_id}/exports/{ex_id}`

Retrieves the details of an existing export. You need only supply the unique export identifier that was returned upon export creation. If you try retrieving an export immediately after creating one (i.e., before we're done processing the export), you will get back an export object with `state = in_progress`.

<h3 id="retrieve-export-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|upl_id|path|[upl_id](#schemaupl_id)|true|ID of the upload|
|ex_id|path|[ex_id](#schemaex_id)|true|ID of the export|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "ex_6a94fe68fd151e0f8",
  "dateCreated": "2021-07-06T22:51:42.838Z",
  "dateModified": "2022-07-06T22:51:42.838Z",
  "deleted": false,
  "s3Url": null,
  "state": "in_progress",
  "type": "failures",
  "uploadId": "upl_71be866e430b11e9"
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-export-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns an export object|Inline|

<h3 id="retrieve-export-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|id|[ex_id](#schemaex_id)|true|none|Unique identifier prefixed with `ex_`.|
|dateCreated|string(date-time)|true|none|A timestamp in ISO 8601 format of the date the export was created|
|dateModified|string(date-time)|true|none|A timestamp in ISO 8601 format of the date the export was last modified|
|deleted|boolean|true|none|Returns as `true` if the resource has been successfully deleted.|
|s3Url|string|true|none|The URL for the generated export file.|
|state|string|true|none|The state of the export file, which can be `in_progress`, `failed` or `succeeded`.|
|type|string|true|none|The export file type, which can be `all`, `failures` or `successes`.|
|uploadId|[upl_id](#schemaupl_id)|true|none|Unique identifier prefixed with `upl_`.|

#### Enumerated Values

|Property|Value|
|---|---|
|state|in_progress|
|state|failed|
|state|succeeded|
|type|all|
|type|failures|
|type|successes|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="lob-url-shortener">URL Shortener</h1>

Lob's URL shortener allows you to generate unique short links, either with Lob's own domain or your own custom domains. Each custom link enables Lob to track mail individually and provide customers the relevant tracking data in their dashboard.

Webhooks can be used to integrate Lob's URL Shortener scans into your omni channel marketing stratergy. See the <a href="#tag/Webhooks">Webhooks</a> section of our documentation to learn how to enable the `letter.viewed`, `postcard.viewed` and `self_mailer.viewed` event notifications for your mail pieces.

Furthermore, you can use our Retrieve endpoints to track the impact and engagement rate of links created.

<a id="opIdlink_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/links \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "redirect_link": "https://www.lob.com",
    "slug": "a1b2c3"
  }'
```

`POST /links`

Given a long URL, shorten your URL either by using a custom domain or Lob's own short domain.

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "redirect_link": "https://www.lob.com",
  "slug": "a1b2c3"
}
```

<h3 id="create-link-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|body|body|[link_single](#schemalink_single)|true|none|
|» title|body|string|false|The title of the URL.|
|» redirect_link|body|[redirect_link](#schemaredirect_link)|true|The original target URL.|
|» domain|body|string|false|The registered domain to be used for the short URL.|
|» slug|body|string|false|The unique path for the shortened URL, if empty a unique path will be used.|
|» metadata|body|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|Use metadata to store custom information for tagging and labeling back to your internal systems. Must be an object with up to 20 key-value pairs. Keys must be at most 40 characters and values must be at most 500 characters. Neither can contain the characters `"` and `\`. i.e. '{"customer_id" : "NEWYORK2015"}' Nested objects are not supported.  See [Metadata](#section/Metadata) for more information.|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "string",
  "title": "string",
  "domain_id": "string",
  "redirect_link": "string",
  "short_link": "string",
  "metadata": {
    "property1": "string",
    "property2": "string"
  },
  "created_at": "string",
  "updated_at": "string"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid",
    "message": "redirect_link is required",
    "status_code": 422
  }
}
```

<h3 id="create-link-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a successfully created link.|[link_response](#schemalink_response)|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

<h1 id="lob-us-autocompletions">US Autocompletions</h1>

Given partial address information, this endpoint returns up to 10 address suggestions. <br> <div class="back-to-top" ><a href="#" onclick="toTopLink()">back to top</a></div>
## Autocompletion Test Env
Your test API key does not autocomplete US addresses and is used to simulate behavior. With your test API key, requests with specific values for `address_prefix` return predetermined values. When `address_prefix` is set to:
- `0 suggestions` - Returns no suggestions - `[PRIMARY NUMBER] s[uggestion]` - Returns a maximum of ten predefined suggested addresses.
  `[PRIMARY NUMBER]` does not have to be a valid primary number when sending a test request.
  Each additional letter in `suggestion` reduces the number of suggestions by one (e.g.
  `1 su` returns 9 suggested addresses). `[PRIMARY NUMBER]` does not affect the number of
  suggestions returned.

City and state filters work as expected and filter the list of predetermined suggested addresses.
See the `test` request & response examples under [Autocomplete Examples](#operation/autocompletion) within the "Autocomplete a partial address" section in US Autocompletions. <div class="back-to-top" ><a href="#" onclick="toTopLink()">back to top</a></div>


## Autocomplete

<a id="opIdautocompletion"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/us_autocompletions \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "address_prefix": "185 B",
    "city": "San Francisco",
    "state": "CA",
    "zip_code": "94107",
    "geo_ip_sort": false
  }'
```

`POST /us_autocompletions`

Given an address prefix consisting of a partial primary line, as well as optional input of city, state, and zip code, this functionality returns up to 10 full US address suggestions. Not all of them will turn out to be valid addresses; they'll need to be [verified](#operation/verification_us).

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "address_prefix": "185 B",
  "city": "San Francisco",
  "state": "CA",
  "zip_code": "94107",
  "geo_ip_sort": false
}
```

<h3 id="autocomplete-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|case|query|string|false|Casing of the verified address. Possible values are `upper` and `proper` for uppercased (e.g. "PO BOX") and proper-cased (e.g. "PO Box"), respectively. Only affects `primary_line`, `city`, and `state`. Default casing is `upper`.|
|valid_addresses|query|boolean|false|Possible values are `true` and `false`. If false, not all of the suggestions in the response will be valid addresses; they'll need to be verified in order to determine the deliverability. The valid_addresses flag will greatly reduce the number of keystrokes needed before reaching an intended address.|
|body|body|[us_autocompletions_writable](#schemaus_autocompletions_writable)|true|none|
|» address_prefix|body|string|true|Only accepts numbers and street names in an alphanumeric format.<br>|
|» city|body|string|false|An optional city input used to filter suggestions. Case insensitive and does not match partial abbreviations.<br>|
|» state|body|string|false|An optional state input used to filter suggestions. Case insensitive and does not match partial abbreviations.<br>|
|» zip_code|body|string|false|An optional ZIP Code input used to filter suggestions. Matches partial entries.<br>|
|» geo_ip_sort|body|boolean|false|If `true`, sort suggestions by proximity to the IP set in the `X-Forwarded-For` header.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|case|upper|
|case|proper|
|valid_addresses|true|
|valid_addresses|false|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "us_auto_a3ac97bcfbb2460ab20c",
  "suggestions": [
    {
      "primary_line": "185 BAYSIDE VILLAGE PL",
      "city": "SAN FRANCISCO",
      "state": "CA",
      "zip_code": "94107"
    },
    {
      "primary_line": "185 BRANNAN ST",
      "city": "SAN FRANCISCO",
      "state": "CA",
      "zip_code": "94107"
    },
    {
      "primary_line": "185 BONIFACIO ST",
      "city": "SAN FRANCISCO",
      "state": "CA",
      "zip_code": "94107"
    },
    {
      "primary_line": "185 BLAIR TER",
      "city": "SAN FRANCISCO",
      "state": "CA",
      "zip_code": "94107"
    },
    {
      "primary_line": "185 BLUXOME ST",
      "city": "SAN FRANCISCO",
      "state": "CA",
      "zip_code": "94107"
    },
    {
      "primary_line": "210 KING ST",
      "city": "SAN FRANCISCO",
      "state": "CA",
      "zip_code": "94107"
    },
    {
      "primary_line": "185 BRYANT ST",
      "city": "SAN FRANCISCO",
      "state": "CA",
      "zip_code": "94107"
    }
  ],
  "object": "us_autocompletion"
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "invalid",
    "message": "address_prefix is required",
    "status_code": 422
  }
}
```

<h3 id="autocomplete-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a US autocompletion object.|[us_autocompletions](#schemaus_autocompletions)|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h1 id="lob-us-verifications">US Verifications</h1>

Validate, automatically correct, and standardize the addresses in your
address book based on USPS's <a href="https://postalpro.usps.com/certifications/cass" target="_blank">Coding Accuracy Support System (CASS)</a>.
<br>
<div class="back-to-top" ><a href="#" onclick="toTopLink()">back to top</a></div>

number for `zip_code` (e.g. "11111") let you explore the responses to many types of addresses:

## Delete

<a id="opIdbooklet_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/booklets/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /booklets/{booklet_id}`

Completely removes a booklet from production. This can only be done if the booklet's `send_date` has not yet passed. If the booklet is successfully canceled, you will not be charged for it.

<h3 id="delete-9-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|booklet_id|path|[booklet_id](#schemabooklet_id)|true|id of the booklet|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "ord_0d6a16a3fff6318ac8f8008dc1",
  "deleted": true
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "not_found",
    "message": "to address not found",
    "status_code": 404
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-9-responses">Responses</h3>

|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Deleted|[booklet_deletion](#schemabooklet_deletion)|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

basicAuth

## List

<a id="opIdbooklets_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/booklets \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /booklets`

Returns a list of your booklets. The booklets are returned sorted by creation date, with the most recently created booklets appearing first.

<h3 id="list-15-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|How many results to return.|
|before/after|query|object|false|`before` and `after` are both optional but only one of them can be in the query at a time.<br>|
|include|query|[string]|false|Request that the response include the total count by specifying `include=["total_count"]`.<br>|
|date_created|query|[date_filter](#schemadate_filter)|false|Filter by date created. Accepted formats are ISO-8601 date or datetime, e.g. `{ "gt": "2012-01-01", "lt": "2012-01-31T12:34:56Z" }` where `gt` is >, `lt` is <, `gte` is ≥, and `lte` is ≤.|
|metadata|query|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|Filter by metadata key-value pair`.|
|send_date|query|[send_date](#schemasend_date)|false|Filter by ISO-8601 date or datetime, e.g. `{ "gt": "2012-01-01", "lt": "2012-01-31T12:34:56Z" }` where `gt` is >, `lt` is <, `gte` is ≥, and `lte` is ≤.<br>|
|mail_type|query|[mail_type](#schemamail_type)|false|A string designating the mail postage type: * `usps_first_class` - (default) * `usps_standard` - a <a href="https://lob.com/pricing/print-mail#compare" target="_blank">cheaper option</a> which is less predictable and takes longer to deliver. `usps_standard` cannot be used with `4x6` postcards or for any postcards sent outside of the United States.<br>|
|sort_by|query|object|false|Sorts items by ascending or descending dates. Use either `date_created` or `send_date`, not both.<br>|
|campaign_id|query|[campaign_id](#schemacampaign_id)|false|Filters resources created by the provided campaign id, prefixed with `cmp_`. In the case of snap packs, booklets, and letters with size `us_legal`, however, the campaign id is prefixed with `camp_` instead of `cmp_`.|
|status|query|[status](#schemastatus)|false|A string describing the render status:<br>* `processed` - the rendering process is currently underway.<br>* `rendered` - the rendering process has completed successfully.<br>* `failed` - the rendering process has failed.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|mail_type|usps_first_class|
|mail_type|usps_standard|
|status|processed|
|status|rendered|
|status|failed|

|200|OK|A dictionary with a data property that contains an array of up to `limit` booklets. Each entry in the array is a separate booklet. The previous and next page of booklets can be retrieved by calling the endpoint contained in the `previous_url` and `next_url` fields in the API response respectively. If no more booklets are available beyond the current set of returned results, the `next_url` field will be empty.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object|[object](#schemaobject)|false|none|Value is resource type.|

|previous_url|string \| null|false|none|Url of previous page of items in list.|
|count|[count](#schemacount)|false|none|number of resources in a set|
|total_count|integer|false|none|Indicates the total number of records. Provided when the request specifies an "include" query parameter|
|data|[[booklet](#schemabooklet)]|false|none|list of booklets|

## Create

<a id="opIdbooklet_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/booklets \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "demo",
    "to": {
      "description": "Harry - Office",
      "name": "Harry Zhang",
      "company": "Lob",
      "email": "harry@lob.com",
      "phone": "5555555555",
      "address_line1": "210 King St",
      "address_line2": "# 6100",
      "address_city": "San Francisco",
      "address_state": "CA",
      "address_zip": "94107",
      "address_country": "US"
    },
    "from": {
      "name": "Harry",
      "address_line1": "210 King St",
      "address_line2": "# 6100",
      "address_city": "San Francisco",
      "address_state": "CA",
      "address_zip": "94107"
    },
    "file": "<html style='\''padding-top: 3in; margin: .5in;'\''>HTML Booklet for {{name}}</html>",
    "mail_type": "usps_first_class",
    "merge_variables": {
      "name": "Harry"
    },
    "metadata": {
      "spiffy": "true"
    },
    "send_date": "2017-11-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "use_type": "marketing",
    "qr_code": {
      "position": "relative",
      "redirect_url": "https://www.lob.com",
      "width": "2",
      "top": "2",
      "right": "2",
      "pages": "1-2,4-5"
    },
    "fsc": true,
    "size": "8.375x5.375",
    "print_speed": "core"
  }'
```

<h3 id="create-18-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|Idempotency-Key|header|string|false|A string of no longer than 256 characters that uniquely identifies this resource. For more help integrating idempotency keys, refer to our <a href="https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/building-a-mail-strategy/managing-mail-settings#idempotent-requests-12" target="_blank">implementation guide</a>.<br>|
|idempotency_key|query|string|false|A string of no longer than 256 characters that uniquely identifies this resource. For more help integrating idempotency keys, refer to our <a href="https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/building-a-mail-strategy/managing-mail-settings#idempotent-requests-12" target="_blank">implementation guide</a>.<br>|
|body|body|[booklet_editable](#schemabooklet_editable)|true|none|
|» to|body|[adr_id](#schemaadr_id) \| [inline_address](#schemainline_address)|true|Must either be an address ID or an inline object with correct address parameters. If an object is used, an address will be created, corrected, and standardized for free whenever possible using our US Address Verification engine (if it is a US address), and returned back with an ID. Depending on your <a href="https://dashboard.lob.com/#/settings/editions" target="_blank">Print & Mail Edition</a>, US addresses may also be run through <a href="#tag/National-Change-of-Address">National Change of Address Linkage(NCOALink)</a>. Non-US addresses will be standardized into uppercase only. If a US address used does not meet your account’s <a href="https://dashboard.lob.com/#/settings/account" target="_blank">US Mail strictness setting</a>, the request will fail. <a href="https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/all-about-addresses" target="_blank">Lob Guide: Verification of Mailing Addresses</a>|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[adr_id](#schemaadr_id)|false|Unique identifier prefixed with `adr_`.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[inline_address](#schemainline_address)|false|none|
|» from|body|[adr_id](#schemaadr_id) \| [inline_address](#schemainline_address)|true|Must either be an address ID or an inline object with correct address parameters. Must be a US address unless using a `custom_envelope`. All addresses will be standardized into uppercase without being modified by verification.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[adr_id](#schemaadr_id)|false|Unique identifier prefixed with `adr_`.|
|» » *oneOf*|body|[inline_address](#schemainline_address)|false|none|
|» description|body|[resource_description](#schemaresource_description)|false|An internal description that identifies this resource. Must be no longer than 255 characters.<br>|
|» metadata|body|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|Use metadata to store custom information for tagging and labeling back to your internal systems. Must be an object with up to 20 key-value pairs. Keys must be at most 40 characters and values must be at most 500 characters. Neither can contain the characters `"` and `\`. i.e. '{"customer_id" : "NEWYORK2015"}' Nested objects are not supported.  See [Metadata](#section/Metadata) for more information.|
|» mail_type|body|[mail_type](#schemamail_type)|false|A string designating the mail postage type:<br>* `usps_first_class` - (default)<br>* `usps_standard` - a <a href="https://lob.com/pricing/print-mail#compare" target="_blank">cheaper option</a> which is<br>less predictable and takes longer to deliver. `usps_standard` cannot be used with `4x6`<br>postcards or for any postcards sent outside of the United States.<br>|
|» merge_variables|body|[merge_variables](#schemamerge_variables)|false|You can input a merge variable payload object to your template or QR code redirect URLs to render dynamic content. For example, if you have a template like: `{{variable_name}}`, pass in `{"variable_name": "Harry"}` to render `Harry`. `merge_variables` must be an object. Any type of value is accepted as long as the object is valid JSON; you can use `strings`, `numbers`, `booleans`, `arrays`, `objects`, or `null`. The max length of the object is 25,000 characters. If you call `JSON.stringify` on your object, it can be no longer than 25,000 characters. Your variable names cannot contain any whitespace or any of the following special characters: `!`, `"`, `#`, `%`, `&`, `'`, `(`, `)`, `*`, `+`, `,`, `/`, `;`, `<`, `=`, `>`, `@`, `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, `` ` ``, `{`, `\|`, `}`, `~`. More instructions can be found in <a href="https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/designing-mail-creatives/dynamic-personalization#using-html-and-merge-variables-10" target="_blank">our guide to using html and merge variables</a>. Depending on your <a href="https://dashboard.lob.com/#/settings/account" target="_blank">Merge Variable strictness</a> setting, if you define variables in your HTML but do not pass them here, you will either receive an error or the variable will render as an empty string. These settings only apply on HTML templates and not on QR code redirect URLs.|
|» send_date|body|[send_date](#schemasend_date)|false|A timestamp in ISO 8601 format which specifies a date after the current time and up to 180 days in the future to send the letter off for production. Setting a send date overrides the default [cancellation window](#section/Cancellation-Windows) applied to the mailpiece. Until the `send_date` has passed, the mailpiece can be canceled. If a date in the format `2017-11-01` is passed, it will evaluate to midnight UTC of that date (`2017-11-01T00:00:00.000Z`). If a datetime is passed, that exact time will be used. A `send_date` passed with no time zone will default to UTC, while a `send_date` passed with a time zone will be converted to UTC.|
|» print_speed|body|[print_speed](#schemaprint_speed)|false|A string designating the mail speed type:<br>* `core` - 2 production business days<br>|
|» file|body|[booklet_file](#schemabooklet_file)|true|Notes:<br>- HTML merge variables should not include delimiting whitespace.<br>- All pages of a supplied PDF file must be sized per the `size` attribute, while supplied HTML will be rendered and trimmed to as many `size` pages as necessary.<br>- For design specifications, please see our <a href="https://s3-us-west-2.amazonaws.com/public.lob.com/assets/templates/letter_template.pdf" target="_blank">PDF</a> and [HTML](#section/HTML-Examples) templates.<br>See <a href="https://lob.com/pricing/print-mail#compare" target="_blank">pricing</a> for extra costs incurred.|
|» mail_type|body|[mail_type](#schemamail_type)|false|A string designating the mail postage type:<br>* `usps_first_class` - (default)<br>* `usps_standard` - a <a href="https://lob.com/pricing/print-mail#compare" target="_blank">cheaper option</a> which is<br>less predictable and takes longer to deliver. `usps_standard` cannot be used with `4x6`<br>postcards or for any postcards sent outside of the United States.<br>|
|» billing_group_id|body|[billing_group_id](#schemabilling_group_id)|false|An optional string with the billing group ID to tag your usage with. Is used for billing purposes. Requires special activation to use. See <a href="#tag/Billing-Groups">Billing Group API</a> for more information.|
|» qr_code|body|[qr_code](#schemaqr_code)|false|Customize and place a QR code on the creative at the required position.|
|» use_type|body|[booklet_use_type](#schemabooklet_use_type)|true|The use type for each mailpiece. Can be one of marketing, operational, or null. Null use_type is only allowed if an account default use_type is selected in Account Settings. For more information on use_type, see our  [Help Center article](https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/building-a-mail-strategy/managing-mail-settings/declaring-mail-use-type).|
|» fsc|body|boolean|false|This is in beta. Contact support@lob.com or your account contact to learn more. Not available for `A4` and `us_legal` letter size.|
|» size|body|[booklet_size](#schemabooklet_size)|true|Specifies the size of the booklet.<br>|
|» pages|body|[booklet_pages](#schemabooklet_pages)|true|Pages specifies the total number of pages in a booklet, where four pages make up one sheet. Pages must always be in increments of four to maintain booklet integrity. For a booklet with dimensions of 8.375x5.375 inches, we allow for 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, or 32 pages.|
|» source_material|body|[booklet_source_material](#schemabooklet_source_material)|false|Defines the material used to create the mail piece, specifically for booklets.  This property is directly tied to the size of the booklet, ensuring that the appropriate material is selected based on the booklet's dimensions. For booklets with `size` equal to `8.375x5.375` inches, the default source material is `60# Gloss Text`.|
|» print_speed|body|[print_speed](#schemaprint_speed)|false|A string designating the mail speed type:<br>* `core` - 2 production business days<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|» mail_type|usps_first_class|
|» mail_type|usps_standard|
|» print_speed|core|
|» mail_type|usps_first_class|
|» mail_type|usps_standard|
|» use_type|marketing|
|» use_type|operational|
|» use_type|null|
|» size|8.375x5.375|
|» source_material|60# Gloss Text|
|» print_speed|core|

<h1 id="lob-snap-packs">Snap Packs</h1>

## Retrieve

<a id="opIdsnap_pack_retrieve"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/snap_packs/string \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /snap_packs/{snap_pack_id}`

Retrieves the details of an existing snap_pack. You need to only supply the unique snap_pack identifier that was returned upon snap_pack creation.

<h3 id="retrieve-19-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|snap_pack_id|path|[snap_pack_id](#schemasnap_pack_id)|true|id of the snap_pack|

> Example responses

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "not_found",
    "message": "to address not found",
    "status_code": 404
  }
}
```

<h3 id="retrieve-19-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Returns a snap_pack object|None|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Delete

<a id="opIdsnap_pack_delete"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/snap_packs/string \
  -X DELETE \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`DELETE /snap_packs/{snap_pack_id}`

Completely removes a snap pack from production. This can only be done if the snap pack's `send_date` has not yet passed. If the snap pack is successfully canceled, you will not be charged for it.

<h3 id="delete-10-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|snap_pack_id|path|[snap_pack_id](#schemasnap_pack_id)|true|id of the snap_pack|

> Example responses

> 200 Response

```json
{
  "id": "ord_0d6a16a3fff6318ac8f8008dc1",
  "deleted": true
}
```

> default Response

```json
{
  "error": {
    "code": "not_found",
    "message": "to address not found",
    "status_code": 404
  }
}
```

<h3 id="delete-10-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|Deleted|[snap_pack_deletion](#schemasnap_pack_deletion)|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## List

<a id="opIdsnap_packs_list"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/snap_packs \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}"
```

`GET /snap_packs`

Returns a list of your snap_packs. The snap_packs are returned sorted by creation date, with the most recently created snap_packs appearing first.

<h3 id="list-16-parameters">Parameters</h3>

|Name|In|Type|Required|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|limit|query|integer|false|How many results to return.|
|before/after|query|object|false|`before` and `after` are both optional but only one of them can be in the query at a time.<br>|
|include|query|[string]|false|Request that the response include the total count by specifying `include=["total_count"]`.<br>|
|date_created|query|[date_filter](#schemadate_filter)|false|Filter by date created. Accepted formats are ISO-8601 date or datetime, e.g. `{ "gt": "2012-01-01", "lt": "2012-01-31T12:34:56Z" }` where `gt` is >, `lt` is <, `gte` is ≥, and `lte` is ≤.|
|metadata|query|[metadata](#schemametadata)|false|Filter by metadata key-value pair`.|
|send_date|query|[send_date](#schemasend_date)|false|Filter by ISO-8601 date or datetime, e.g. `{ "gt": "2012-01-01", "lt": "2012-01-31T12:34:56Z" }` where `gt` is >, `lt` is <, `gte` is ≥, and `lte` is ≤.<br>|
|mail_type|query|[mail_type](#schemamail_type)|false|A string designating the mail postage type: * `usps_first_class` - (default) * `usps_standard` - a <a href="https://lob.com/pricing/print-mail#compare" target="_blank">cheaper option</a> which is less predictable and takes longer to deliver. `usps_standard` cannot be used with `4x6` postcards or for any postcards sent outside of the United States.<br>|
|sort_by|query|object|false|Sorts items by ascending or descending dates. Use either `date_created` or `send_date`, not both.<br>|
|campaign_id|query|[campaign_id](#schemacampaign_id)|false|Filters resources created by the provided campaign id, prefixed with `cmp_`. In the case of snap packs, booklets, and letters with size `us_legal`, however, the campaign id is prefixed with `camp_` instead of `cmp_`.|
|status|query|[status](#schemastatus)|false|A string describing the render status:<br>* `processed` - the rendering process is currently underway.<br>* `rendered` - the rendering process has completed successfully.<br>* `failed` - the rendering process has failed.<br>|

#### Enumerated Values

|Parameter|Value|
|---|---|
|mail_type|usps_first_class|
|mail_type|usps_standard|
|status|processed|
|status|rendered|
|status|failed|

<h3 id="list-16-responses">Responses</h3>

|Status|Meaning|Description|Schema|
|---|---|---|---|
|200|OK|A dictionary with a data property that contains an array of up to `limit` snap_packs. Each entry in the array is a separate self_mailer. The previous and next page of snap_packs can be retrieved by calling the endpoint contained in the `previous_url` and `next_url` fields in the API response respectively.<br>If no more snap_packs are available beyond the current set of returned results, the `next_url` field will be empty.|Inline|
|default|Default|Error|[error](#schemaerror)|

<h3 id="list-16-responseschema">Response Schema</h3>

Status Code **200**

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|object|[object](#schemaobject)|false|none|Value is resource type.|
|next_url|string \| null|false|none|Url of next page of items in list.|
|previous_url|string \| null|false|none|Url of previous page of items in list.|
|count|[count](#schemacount)|false|none|number of resources in a set|
|total_count|integer|false|none|Indicates the total number of records. Provided when the request specifies an "include" query parameter|
|data|[[snap_pack](#schemasnap_pack)]|false|none|list of snap_packs|

<aside class="warning">
To perform this operation, you must be authenticated by means of one of the following methods:
basicAuth
</aside>

## Create

<a id="opIdsnap_pack_create"></a>

> Code samples

```bash
curl https://api.lob.com/v1/snap_packs \
  -X POST \
  -H 'Content-Type: application/json' \
  -H 'Accept: application/json' \
  -H "Authorization: Basic ${CREDENTIALS}" \
  -d '{
    "description": "Demo Snap Pack Job",
    "to": "adr_bae820679f3f536b",
    "from": "adr_210a8d4b0b76d77b",
    "inside": "https://lob.com/snappackinside.pdf",
    "outside": "https://lob.com/snappackoutside.pdf",
    "size": "8.5x11",
    "metadata": {
      "spiffy": "true"
    },
    "mail_type": "usps_standard",
    "merge_variables": {
      "name": "Harry"
    },
    "send_date": "2017-11-01T00:00:00.000Z",
    "use_type": "marketing",
    "print_speed": "core"
  }'
```

`POST /snap_packs`

Creates a new snap_pack given information

> Body parameter

```json
{
  "description": "Demo Snap Pack Job",
  "to": "adr_bae820679f3f536b",
  "from": "adr_210a8d4b0b76d77b",
  "inside": "https://lob.com/snappackinside.pdf",
  "outside": "https://lob.com/snappackoutside.pdf",
  "size": "8.5x11",
  "metadata": {
    "spiffy": "true"
  },

Any type of value is accepted as long as the object is valid JSON; you can use `strings`, `numbers`, `booleans`, `arrays`, `objects`, or `null`. The max length of the object is 25,000 characters. Your variable names cannot contain any whitespace or any of the following special characters: `!`, `"`, `#`, `%`, `&`, `'`, `(`, `)`, `*`, `+`, `,`, `/`, `;`, `<`, `=`, `>`, `@`, `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, `` ` ``, `{`, `\|`, `}`, `~`. If a date in the format `2017-11-01` is passed, it will evaluate to midnight UTC of that date (`2017-11-01T00:00:00.000Z`). If a datetime is passed, that exact time will be used. ```

A conventional HTTP status code:
  * `401` - Authorization error with your API key or account
  * `403` - Forbidden error with your API key or account
  * `404` - The requested item does not exist
  * `413` - Payload too large
  * `422` - The query or body parameters did not pass validation
  * `429` - Too many requests have been sent with an API key in a given amount of time
  * `500` - An internal server error occurred, please contact support@lob.com

If both `name` and `company` are provided, they will be printed on two separate lines above the rest of the address. This field can be used for any secondary recipient information which is not part of the actual mailing address (Company Name, Department, Attention Line, etc).

### Properties

|name|string|true|none|Name of tracking event (for normal postcards, self mailers, letters, checks and snap packs):<br><br>  * `Mailed` - The mailpiece has been handed off to and accepted by USPS<br>    and is en route. <a href="https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/getting-data-and-results/tracking-your-mail#mailed-tracking-events-4" target="_blank">More about<br>    Mailed.</a><br>    Note this data is only available in Enterprise editions of<br>    Lob. <a href="https://lob.com/support/contact#contact" target="_blank">Contact Sales</a> if<br>    you want access to this feature.<br><br>  * `In Transit` - The mailpiece is being processed at the entry/origin facility.<br><br>  * `In Local Area` - The mailpiece is being processed at the destination facility.<br><br>  * `Processed for Delivery` - The mailpiece has been greenlit for<br>    delivery at the recipient's nearest postal facility. The mailpiece<br>    should reach the mailbox within 1 business day of this tracking<br>    event.<br><br>  * `Delivered` - The mail piece has been delivered to <br>    the recipient’s address. The final scan is generated when the mail <br>    carrier's GPS unit leaves the delivery area.<br><br>  * `Re-Routed` - The mailpiece is re-routed due to recipient change of<br>    address, address errors, or USPS relabeling of barcode/ID tag<br>    area.<br><br>  * `Returned to Sender` - The mailpiece is being returned to sender due<br>    to barcode, ID tag area, or address errors.<br>  <br>  * `International Exit` - The mail piece has been processed to <br>    ship to a destination abroad. This is typically the last <br>    scan a US-originated international mail piece will receive <br>    from the USPS.<br><br><a href="https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/getting-data-and-results/tracking-your-mail#mailed-tracking-events-4" target="_blank">More about tracking</a><br>|
|details|object \| null|false|none|Will be `null` for `type=normal` events|
|location|string \| null|false|none|The zip code in which the scan event occurred. Null for `Mailed` events.<br>|

|name|International Exit|
|details|null|

<h2 id="tocS_merge_variables">merge_variables</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemamerge_variables"></a>
<a id="schema_merge_variables"></a>
<a id="tocSmerge_variables"></a>
<a id="tocsmerge_variables"></a>

```json
{}
```

You can input a merge variable payload object to your template or QR code redirect URLs to render dynamic content. For example, if you have a template like: `{{variable_name}}`, pass in `{"variable_name": "Harry"}` to render `Harry`. `merge_variables` must be an object. Any type of value is accepted as long as the object is valid JSON; you can use `strings`, `numbers`, `booleans`, `arrays`, `objects`, or `null`. The max length of the object is 25,000 characters. If you call `JSON.stringify` on your object, it can be no longer than 25,000 characters. Your variable names cannot contain any whitespace or any of the following special characters: `!`, `"`, `#`, `%`, `&`, `'`, `(`, `)`, `*`, `+`, `,`, `/`, `;`, `<`, `=`, `>`, `@`, `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, `` ` ``, `{`, `|`, `}`, `~`. More instructions can be found in <a href="https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/designing-mail-creatives/dynamic-personalization#using-html-and-merge-variables-10" target="_blank">our guide to using html and merge variables</a>. Depending on your <a href="https://dashboard.lob.com/#/settings/account" target="_blank">Merge Variable strictness</a> setting, if you define variables in your HTML but do not pass them here, you will either receive an error or the variable will render as an empty string. These settings only apply on HTML templates and not on QR code redirect URLs.

<h2 id="tocS_send_date">send_date</h2>
<!-- backwards compatibility -->
<a id="schemasend_date"></a>
<a id="schema_send_date"></a>
<a id="tocSsend_date"></a>
<a id="tocssend_date"></a>

```json
null
```

A timestamp in ISO 8601 format which specifies a date after the current time and up to 180 days in the future to send the letter off for production. Setting a send date overrides the default [cancellation window](#section/Cancellation-Windows) applied to the mailpiece. Until the `send_date` has passed, the mailpiece can be canceled. If a date in the format `2017-11-01` is passed, it will evaluate to midnight UTC of that date (`2017-11-01T00:00:00.000Z`). If a datetime is passed, that exact time will be used. A `send_date` passed with no time zone will default to UTC, while a `send_date` passed with a time zone will be converted to UTC.

### Properties

|Name|Type|Required|Restrictions|Description|
|---|---|---|---|---|
|*anyOf*|object(date-time)|false|none|none|
|*anyOf*|object(date)|false|none|none|

```

A string designating the mail postage type:
* `usps_first_class` - (default)
* `usps_standard` - a <a href="https://lob.com/pricing/print-mail#compare" target="_blank">cheaper option</a> which is
less predictable and takes longer to deliver. `usps_standard` cannot be used with `4x6`
postcards or for any postcards sent outside of the United States.

<h2 id="tocS_booklet_pages">booklet_pages</h2>

<a id="tocSbooklet_pages"></a>
<a id="tocsbooklet_pages"></a>

```json
0
```

Pages specifies the total number of pages in a booklet, where four pages make up one sheet. Pages must always be in increments of four to maintain booklet integrity. For a booklet with dimensions of 8.375x5.375 inches, we allow for 8, 12, 16, 20, 24, 28, or 32 pages.

<a id="tocsstatus"></a>

```json
"processed"
```

A string describing the PDF render status:
* `processed` - the rendering process is currently in progress.
* `rendered` - a PDF has been successfully rendered of the mailpiece.
* `failed` - one or more issues has caused the rendering process to fail.

<h2 id="tocS_booklet_source_material">booklet_source_material</h2>

<a id="tocSbooklet_source_material"></a>
<a id="tocsbooklet_source_material"></a>

```json
"60# Gloss Text"
```

Defines the material used to create the mail piece, specifically for booklets.  This property is directly tied to the size of the booklet, ensuring that the appropriate material is selected based on the booklet's dimensions. For booklets with `size` equal to `8.375x5.375` inches, the default source material is `60# Gloss Text`.

Any type of value is accepted as long as the object is valid JSON; you can use `strings`, `numbers`, `booleans`, `arrays`, `objects`, or `null`. The max length of the object is 25,000 characters. If you call `JSON.stringify` on your object, it can be no longer than 25,000 characters. Your variable names cannot contain any whitespace or any of the following special characters: `!`, `"`, `#`, `%`, `&`, `'`, `(`, `)`, `*`, `+`, `,`, `/`, `;`, `<`, `=`, `>`, `@`, `[`, `\`, `]`, `^`, `` ` ``, `{`, `\|`, `}`, `~`. Depending on your <a href="https://dashboard.lob.com/#/settings/account" target="_blank">Merge Variable strictness</a> setting, if you define variables in your HTML but do not pass them here, you will either receive an error or the variable will render as an empty string. A `send_date` passed with no time zone will default to UTC, while a `send_date` passed with a time zone will be converted to UTC.|

Null use_type is only allowed if an account default use_type is selected in Account Settings. For more information on use_type, see our  [Help Center article](https://help.lob.com/print-and-mail/building-a-mail-strategy/managing-mail-settings/declaring-mail-use-type).|

|fsc|boolean|false|none|This is in beta. Contact support@lob.com or your account contact to learn more.|
|status|[status](#schemastatus)|false|none|A string describing the PDF render status:<br>* `processed` - the rendering process is currently in progress.<br>* `rendered` - a PDF has been successfully rendered of the mailpiece.<br>* `failed` - one or more issues has caused the rendering process to fail.<br>|

For booklets with `size` equal to `8.375x5.375` inches, the default source material is `60# Gloss Text`.|
